title: Bitcoin AI Model Review — Week 33: 3 of 6 Calls Correct
meta_description: Week 33 graded: 3 of 6 Bitcoin calls correct (50%). All-time: 45.5% over 11 public calls. Paper portfolio -3.5% vs holding.

intro: Welcome to the weekly recap for week 33, covering the date range 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-15.
The model resolved 6 calls this week, landing 3 hits and 3 misses for an even 50.0 percent accuracy.
The week split into two halves, opening with clean calls before sliding into an active streak of 3 misses.
days: The week began on Monday with a hold signal at 57.8 percent confidence, which proved correct as price moved negative 0.97 percent.
On Tuesday the model issued another hold at 68 percent confidence, logging a hit against a negative 0.6 percent move.
Wednesday continued the winning run with a hold at 63.3 percent confidence over a 0.15 percent change.
Late in the week the model flipped its posture to sell signals that missed entirely.
Friday produced a sell call at 75.8 percent confidence against a 0.69 percent gain, and Saturday ended with a sell at 57.6 percent confidence during a 0.03 percent move.
spotlight: The notable miss of the week occurred on Thursday, 2026-08-13.
The model issued a hold call with 59.4 percent confidence.
Bitcoin dropped negative 1.88 percent over the 24 hour horizon, breaking past the 1.0 percent flat band.
That graded as an outright miss and broke the model's opening run.
trend: Price action stayed relatively quiet during the early session before taking a sharper dip on Thursday.
The subsequent rebound on Friday and flat Saturday trading caught the model leaning short, turning both late sell calls into failed predictions.
portfolio: The paper portfolio started with 10000.0 dollars and is now valued at 9646.61 dollars after 12 days, sitting in cash.
That represents a return of negative 3.53 percent across 2 trades with 29.49 dollars paid in fees.
A simple buy and hold strategy sits at 9743.19 dollars or negative 2.57 percent, meaning following the model trailed holding by negative 0.97 percent.
record: Across the entire history, the all time record stands at 5 hits and 6 misses over 11 resolved calls, giving an accuracy of 45.5 percent.
Hold calls have carried the system with 71.4 percent accuracy across 7 signals, while buy and sell signals each remain at 0.0 percent accuracy over 2 calls each.
With only 11 resolved calls on record, this remains a very small sample size that is performing below a coin flip.

research.title: Four architectures, one vote
paragraphs: The ensemble mixes four model families on purpose. They read the market differently, so they fail differently.
When their votes are blended, one model's blind spot is another model's signal. Disagreement between them is information, not a bug.
None of the four is the best model. Picking a favourite would mean betting everything on one way of being wrong.
